cases.question: Which data system do you use for delays?

runs.answer: Delays in the Capacity Pressure Score come from the BTS Airline On-Time Performance dataset (ontime). It covers domestic reporting carriers, from January 2023 to December 2025 (202301..202512), and also supplies taxi-out times. Live conditions such as ground stops and arrival or departure delays come from a separate source, the FAA NAS status feed. That feed is not part of the score.

Delays in the Capacity Pressure Score come from the BTS Airline On-Time Performance dataset (called "ontime" here). It covers domestic reporting carriers and includes delays and taxi-out times. The snapshot runs from January 2023 to December 2025 (202301..202512). For what is happening at an airport right now, such as ground stops or delay programs, I use the FAA NAS status feed. That feed is separate from the frozen score.

cases.question: What rules decide whether a flight counts as long haul?

runs.answer: A flight counts as long haul when its stage length is 3,000 miles or more. The long-haul share is the portion of an airport's departures that meet that threshold. It comes from BTS T-100 Segment data, which covers all carriers. I can't give more detail on how the distance is assigned. I can pull the long-haul share for a specific airport, or rank airports on the long_haul lens, if you want that.

A flight counts as long haul when its segment is 3,000 miles or more. The airport's long-haul share is its departures of 3,000+ miles divided by all its departures. The tool's long_haul_miles threshold is 3000. As an example, JFK had 52,786 long-haul departures out of 220,185 total departures in 2025, a long-haul share of 24.0%. The data comes from BTS T-100 segment records for all carriers, including cargo. Long haul carries a 10% weight in the Capacity Pressure Score.

cases.question: Can an analyst override the weights, or are they fixed in the config?

runs.answer: I can't confirm whether an analyst can override the weights. None of the tools I have exposes a weight-override option, and none describes how the config is managed. What the tools do show is that scoring version 1.1.0 applies one set of weights to every airport: utilization 0.3, delay 0.25, growth 0.2, load factor 0.15 and long haul 0.1. The ATL score breakdown reports these same weights. I can't change them in a query, so any custom weighting would have to happen outside this assistant. The tool output calls the weights and thresholds stated assumptions, not calibrated to investment outcomes.
